payload.stem: A random sample of $22$ light bulbs gives a $90\%$ confidence interval of $(894.1, 937.9)$ for $\mu$, the mean lifetime, in hours, of all light bulbs of one brand. The same sample is used to test $H_0: \mu = 912.2$ against $H_a: \mu > 912.2$ at significance level $\alpha = 0.05$. Assume that the conditions for inference are met. Which of the following is a correct conclusion?

options.text: Reject $H_0$; there is convincing evidence that $\mu < 912.2$
options.why: Rejects in the direction opposite to the alternative hypothesis, and $912.2$ lies inside $(894.1, 937.9)$, so $H_0$ is not rejected at all.

options.text: Reject $H_0$; there is convincing evidence that $\mu > 912.2$
options.why: Places $912.2$ outside the interval, but it lies inside $(894.1, 937.9)$.

options.text: No conclusion can be reached, because a confidence interval cannot be used to carry out a significance test
options.why: Treats the interval and the test as unrelated, but a two-sided interval at confidence level $1-2\alpha$ gives the decision for a test at level $\alpha$ in the direction supported by the interval.

options.text: Fail to reject $H_0$; there is not convincing evidence that $\mu > 912.2$
options.why: A $90\%$ two-sided interval matches a one-sided test at $\alpha = 0.05$; $912.2$ lies inside the interval, so the sample gives no support for $H_a$ and $H_0$ is not rejected (the P-value is about $0.384$).
